project.name: The Eye and Sickle :: Solo runtime
project.description:
The single-player runtime: an in-process, offline rules engine with a plain JSON save file.
WHY THIS MODULE EXISTS. The game must be playable with no internet, no account and no PostgreSQL (docs/design/00 — "single-player by default"). The obvious implementation — start the real Spring server locally against an embedded database — is not available and would be expensive if it were:
* client/pom.xml bans eyeandsickle-server, Spring, Postgres and Flyway TRANSITIVELY. That ban is Invariant I14 made mechanical and is not something to route around. * The schema is deeply PostgreSQL-coupled (37 jsonb columns, uuid, now()), so an H2 swap is a porting project, not a config switch. * A second JVM running Boot costs roughly 200 MB of RSS, ~80 MB of jars and several seconds of startup, for a mode whose whole appeal is that you double-click and play.
So single player runs here: pure Java, no framework, no driver, no port, no daemon. The footprint is the save file.
THE INVARIANT THIS PRESERVES. I14 says game state never lives on player-controlled infrastructure. A solo save lives exactly there — so a solo character is LOCAL-ONLY AND CAN NEVER FEDERATE. Nothing minted here has a route into the federated economy, which is the property I14 exists to guarantee. docs/architecture/02 §4 recommends precisely this split ("local identity for solo play; a DID is required only to join a federated server"). Going online means a character created on a real home server, not an export of this one.
THE COST, STATED PLAINLY. This is a second implementation of a subset of the game's rules. That duplication is real and it is the price of the small footprint; see Balance, which cites the design doc for every number so drift is at least visible, and SOLO-1 in docs/design/15-open-questions.

bannedDependencies.message:
The solo runtime is a plain library, not a second server.
It must not acquire Spring, a database driver, a migration tool or an HTTP stack. The moment it does, the "no second process, no database" property that justifies this module's existence is gone, and the honest move would be to launch the real server instead.
It must also never depend on eyeandsickle-client: rules do not import a view layer.
